# Translate Foreign Documents and Everyday Signs with Gemini

**Hook:** Point your phone at a Japanese menu, a French letter or a German street sign, and Gemini can read it, translate it, and answer your follow-up questions — all in plain English. This guide shows you exactly how, even if you've never opened the app before.

## Before you start
- A **Google account** (the same one you use for Gmail or YouTube works).
- The **free Gemini app** on your phone (iOS or Android) — or you can use the website at `gemini.google.com`. The free plan is enough for translation, though a paid plan (Google AI Pro / Advanced) gives access to more capable models.
- A **smartphone with a working camera** is the easiest way. A computer with a webcam also works.
- Allow **2-5 minutes** for your first try. Photos with clear lighting and steady hands give the best results.

## Step 1 — Open the Gemini app and start a fresh chat
Tap the **Gemini app icon** on your home screen — it looks like a four-pointed star in blue, pink and white. If you can't find it, swipe up to open your app drawer and search "Gemini". If you only have a computer, open your browser and go to `gemini.google.com`. The screen that loads is a chat window with a text box at the bottom, a greeting like *"Hello, how can I help?"*, and either a "+" button or a camera icon nearby.

💬 Example: (none in this step)

You'll know it worked when you see the chat box ready for input and no error messages.

## Step 2 — Attach a photo of the sign, menu, or document
Look at the **left side of the text box** for a small **camera icon** 📷 or a **"+" button**. Tap it, and a small menu slides up with two choices: **"Camera"** (to snap a new photo) and **"Photos"** or **"Gallery"** (to pick an existing one). Hold your phone flat and steady over the text — try to fill the frame with the document. If you can't see a camera icon, look for a paperclip or attachment symbol — different phone versions sometimes tuck it in a different spot.

💬 Example: (no typing yet)

You'll know it worked when a small **thumbnail of your photo** appears next to the text box, waiting to be sent.

## Step 3 — Ask Gemini to translate the photo
With the photo attached, **tap into the text box** and write what you want. Be specific about both the language and what you need — *"translate to English"* is a good start, but adding extra questions gets more useful answers. Then tap the **send button** — usually a paper plane icon ✈️ at the right edge of the box. Gemini will take a few seconds to "read" the image, then reply with both the translation and any extra notes you asked for.

💬 Example: "Translate this menu to English. After the translation, list the three cheapest main courses and tell me which ones are likely vegetarian."

You'll know it worked when you see a translated version of the text in the chat, in plain English, within about 10-20 seconds.

## Step 4 — Read the result and ask follow-up questions
The first reply usually gives you a clean translation. Scroll through it. If a dish name, sign or letter still feels unclear, **ask another question in the same chat** — your photo stays attached, so Gemini keeps using it as context. This is where Gemini shines compared to a basic translation app: you can ask things like *"what's the spiciest option?"* or *"summarise what this letter is asking me to do"* without uploading anything new.

💬 Example: "What does the word 'konbini' mean here, and is the dish at the top of the page likely to contain nuts?"

You'll know it worked when Gemini answers your new question using the same photo as context — without you needing to send it again.

## Step 5 — Try Gemini Live for hands-free, real-time translation
For signs or menus you want to read **on the spot** (while standing in front of them), Gemini Live lets you point your camera and talk. Look for a **waveform icon** 🌊 or a **"Live" button** near the bottom-right of the screen. Tap it, grant camera and microphone access if asked, and the viewfinder opens. Hold your phone towards the sign and speak your question out loud. Gemini will listen, look, and answer back in a natural voice — no typing needed.

💬 Example: (say this out loud) "I'm looking at a Japanese train station sign — what does it say, and which platform do I need for Shinjuku?"

You'll know it worked when Gemini **speaks the translation back to you** while the camera stays open. If it can't find the right words, just say *"try again"* or rephrase your question.

## Common mistakes
- **Photo is blurry or angled.** Fix: hold the phone flat, fill the frame, and tap-to-focus before snapping. Good lighting matters more than a fancy camera.
- **You ask for translation but skip the language.** Fix: always say *"translate to English"* — without it, Gemini may reply in the original language.
- **You expect 100% accuracy on handwritten notes.** Fix: typed text and printed signs translate best; handwriting, very old fonts, and crumpled paper can confuse the AI. Treat the result as a helpful first pass, not a legal translation.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** Travel becomes less stressful — you can read street signs, restaurant menus, train tickets and even letters from family overseas without fumbling through a phrasebook.
- **For your work or work:** Translate customer emails, product labels, supplier invoices or international contracts for a first read — then bring the important ones to a human translator for sign-off.
- **If you're just getting started:** Pick **one thing in another language** sitting in your house right now — an old letter, a product label, a souvenir menu — and run it through Step 3 tonight.

## What Gemini *cannot* do here
A clear honest note: Gemini **reads and translates the image**, but it is not a certified translator. For legal documents, immigration papers, medical instructions or anything with real consequences, treat the output as a draft and verify with a qualified human translator before acting on it.

## Try it now
In the next two minutes: open the Gemini app, snap a photo of any piece of text you can see right now — a cereal box, a bill, a sign out the window — and ask *"translate to English and summarise the key points"*. You'll have your first translation before your cup of tea is ready.
